name: Rating
description: Shows a score as a row of stars or similar symbols, or lets people choose one. Use the display version for averages and reviews, and the input version in review forms.
summary: Shows or collects a score, usually as stars
htmlElement: Display: text with a text alternative. Input: <fieldset> with radio inputs

elements.name: Symbols
elements.description: Stars or other icons, filled up to the score; hidden from screen readers

elements.name: Value text
elements.description: The score as text, such as "4.2 out of 5"

elements.name: Count
elements.description: Number of ratings, often a link to the reviews

elements.name: Legend
elements.description: Names what is being rated; required in the input version

configOptions.options: Full row, Single star with value

variants.caption: Value and count — text after the stars
Single star — one star with the value

usageNotes: There is no native rating element. For display, give the whole rating one text alternative, such as visually hidden text "4 out of 5 stars", and hide the individual symbols with aria-hidden="true". An aria-label on a plain <p> or <span> isn't reliably announced.
For input, use a <fieldset> with a <legend> and one radio input per score, each labeled like "3 stars". Arrow keys and screen readers then work without extra scripting.
Filled and empty stars must differ by more than color, such as solid versus outline shapes (WCAG 1.4.1 Use of Color). Showing the number as text helps too.
Show the scale ("out of 5") and, where it matters, the number of ratings, so a perfect score from two people isn't read as strong evidence.
In the input version, make each star at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels (WCAG 2.5.8 Target Size, Minimum).
